title: Bladder diary
what: For a few days at home, you write down how much you drink and when you use the toilet. Sometimes also how much urine you pass each time.
why: For frequent urges, getting up at night to pee, or leaking. The diary shows the doctor things that are hard to remember.
duration: usually 2 to 3 days of notes; it is reviewed at your visit
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially water pills
If writing things down is hard, say so. The doctor will suggest an easier way

prepare.title: Form
prepare.text: Get a form from your doctor or draw columns in a notebook: time, how much you drank, how much urine, any urges or leaking.

prepare.title: Measuring cup
prepare.text: You need a measuring cup or jar with markings. Pee into it and write down the amount.

prepare.title: Days
prepare.text: Choose normal days when you are at home. Drink and go about your day as usual.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: In the morning, note the time you get up
Each time you drink, write down the time and how much
Each time you use the toilet, write down the time and the amount of urine
Mark any strong urges and leaking
Write down getting up at night too
Give the diary to the doctor at your visit
feel: The first day feels like a hassle, then you get used to it
It can feel awkward, but the doctor needs honest numbers
after: Bring the diary to your visit
The doctor will review it and tell you what to do next

faq.q: Should I drink more or less than usual?
faq.a: No. Drink as usual, or the diary will not show your real picture.

faq.q: What if I missed an entry?
faq.a: That is OK. Mark the gap and keep going.

reminders.text: You start your bladder diary tomorrow. Get the form and a measuring cup ready.
